prompt.adult: Deborah was judging Israel in the days of Jabin. Besides a judge, what does the Bible call her?
prompt.child: Deborah led Israel as a judge. What else does the Bible say she was?
prompt.teen: What role does Judges 4 give Deborah, along with judging Israel at that time?
prompt.older: According to Judges 4:4, what was Deborah besides one who judged Israel?

verses.text: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, was judging Israel at that time.

explanation.adult: Judges 4:4 describes Deborah right after her name.
explanation.child: Read Judges 4:4. Look at the words right after "Deborah."
explanation.teen: Judges 4:4 gives her name, a title, and her husband's name. Find the title.
explanation.older: Judges 4:4 introduces Deborah with a title and a family note before saying she was judging Israel.

teaching.extended_explanation: Judges 4:4 introduces Deborah with a title before it says she was judging Israel. Read the verse again.
teaching.takeaway: Deborah was a prophetess who judged Israel.

review.notes: Rooted stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _rooted_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Where would Deborah sit when the children of Israel came to her for judgment?
prompt.child: People in Israel came to Deborah to settle their problems. Where did she sit?
prompt.teen: When Israelites needed Deborah to judge a matter, where did they find her?
prompt.older: According to Judges 4:5, where would Deborah sit?

verses.text: And she would sit under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the mountains of Ephraim. And the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.

explanation.adult: Judges 4:5 begins by telling where she would sit.
explanation.child: Read the first sentence of Judges 4:5.
explanation.teen: Judges 4:5 names a tree that even carried her name.
explanation.older: Judges 4:5 gives her seat and its location between Ramah and Bethel.

teaching.extended_explanation: Deborah had a known place where people came to her. Judges 4:5 names it. Read the first part of the verse.
teaching.takeaway: Deborah sat under the palm tree of Deborah to judge Israel.

review.notes: Rooted stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _rooted_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Jabin king of Canaan harshly oppressed Israel for twenty years. How many chariots of iron did he have?
prompt.child: King Jabin made life hard for Israel. How many iron chariots did he have?
prompt.teen: Israel cried out to the LORD because of King Jabin's army. How many chariots of iron did Jabin own?
prompt.older: According to Judges 4:3, how many chariots of iron did Jabin have?

verses.text: And the children of Israel cried out to the LORD; for Jabin had nine hundred chariots of iron, and for twenty years he had harshly oppressed the children of Israel.

explanation.adult: Judges 4:3 gives the reason Israel cried out. Read the number before "chariots of iron."
explanation.child: Read Judges 4:3. The number of chariots is in the middle.
explanation.teen: Judges 4:3 tells why Israel cried out to the LORD. Find how many chariots there were.
explanation.older: Judges 4:3 gives two reasons for Israel's cry: the size of Jabin's chariot force and the length of the oppression.

teaching.extended_explanation: Israel was facing a powerful army. Judges 4:3 says how many iron chariots Jabin had. Read the verse again.
teaching.takeaway: Jabin had nine hundred chariots of iron.

review.notes: Rooted stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _rooted_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: Barak said he would not go to battle unless Deborah went with him. Because of this, into whose hand did Deborah say the LORD would sell Sisera?
prompt.child: Barak would only go if Deborah went too. So Deborah said Sisera would be given to someone else. Who?
prompt.teen: Since Barak insisted that Deborah come along, she said the glory would not be his. Into whose hand would the LORD sell Sisera?
prompt.older: Per Judges 4:8-9, what was the result of Barak's condition? Into whose hand would the LORD sell Sisera?

verses.text: And Barak said to her, “If you will go with me, then I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go!”

So she said, “I will surely go with you; nevertheless there will be no glory for you in the journey you are taking, for the LORD will sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.” Then Deborah arose and went with Barak to Kedesh.

explanation.adult: Judges 4:8 gives Barak's condition, and Judges 4:9 tells what Deborah said would happen because of it.
explanation.child: Read the end of Deborah's words in Judges 4:9.
explanation.teen: Judges 4:9 says there would be no glory for Barak. Read the reason that follows.
explanation.older: Deborah agrees in Judges 4:9 but adds a consequence; the last words of her speech name who would receive Sisera.

teaching.extended_explanation: Deborah agreed to go, but she said the honor would go to someone other than Barak. Read the end of her words in Judges 4:9.
teaching.takeaway: Deborah said the LORD would sell Sisera into the hand of a woman.

review.notes: Rooted stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _rooted_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: At the end of their song, Deborah and Barak prayed that those who love the LORD would be like what?
prompt.child: Deborah and Barak sang a song after the battle. They said people who love God should be like something bright. What was it?
prompt.teen: The song of Deborah and Barak ends by comparing those who love the LORD to something. What?
prompt.older: In Judges 5:31, those who love the LORD are compared to what?

verses.text: “Thus let all Your enemies perish, O LORD! But let those who love Him be like the sun When it comes out in full strength.” So the land had rest for forty years.

explanation.adult: Judges 5:31 ends the song with a comparison. Read the words after "be like."
explanation.child: Read the second sentence of Judges 5:31.
explanation.teen: Judges 5:31 contrasts the LORD's enemies with those who love Him. Find what the second group is compared to.
explanation.older: The closing couplet of the song in Judges 5:31 uses an image of something rising in full strength.

teaching.extended_explanation: The song closes with a picture of the people who love the LORD. Judges 5:31 names it. Read the verse again.
teaching.takeaway: The song prays that those who love the LORD will be like the sun rising in full strength.

review.notes: Rooted stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _rooted_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: When the LORD routed Sisera's chariots and army before Barak, what did Sisera himself do?
prompt.child: God made Sisera's army fall apart in front of Barak. What did Sisera do then?
prompt.teen: As his army was routed, how did Sisera, the enemy commander, try to escape?
prompt.older: According to Judges 4:15, what did Sisera do when the LORD routed his army?

verses.text: And the LORD routed Sisera and all his chariots and all his army with the edge of the sword before Barak; and Sisera alighted from his chariot and fled away on foot.

explanation.adult: Judges 4:15 tells what Sisera did after he got down from his chariot.
explanation.teen: Judges 4:15 says Sisera alighted from his chariot. Read what he did next.
explanation.older: Judges 4:15 records the rout and then Sisera's own response; the last clause gives it.

teaching.extended_explanation: The LORD gave Barak the victory, and Sisera left his chariot behind. Read the end of Judges 4:15 again.
teaching.takeaway: Sisera got down from his chariot and fled away on foot.

review.notes: Rooted stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _rooted_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: After the battle, Sisera went to the tent of a family that was at peace with his king. Whose tent was it?
prompt.child: After the battle, Sisera went to someone's tent to hide. Whose tent was it?
prompt.teen: Sisera thought he would be safe because Heber's house had peace with Jabin. To whose tent did he go?
prompt.older: According to Judges 4:17, to whose tent did Sisera go?

verses.text: However, Sisera had fled away on foot to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite; for there was peace between Jabin king of Hazor and the house of Heber the Kenite.

explanation.adult: Judges 4:17 names the owner of the tent and says whose wife she was.
explanation.child: Read Judges 4:17. Look for the name before "the wife of Heber."
explanation.teen: Judges 4:17 explains why Sisera felt safe there and names the owner of the tent.
explanation.older: Judges 4:17 names her, gives her husband Heber the Kenite, and explains the peace between Heber's house and Jabin.

teaching.extended_explanation: Sisera went to a tent where he expected to be safe. Judges 4:17 names the one who lived there. Read it again.
teaching.takeaway: Sisera went to the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite, and the LORD gave Israel the victory.

prompt.adult: Chapter 4 says Sisera gathered his chariots for battle. According to the song in chapter 5, what swept his forces away?
prompt.child: Sisera brought all his chariots to fight Israel. In their song, Deborah and Barak tell what washed his army away. What was it?
prompt.teen: The story in Judges 4 and the song in Judges 5 describe the same battle. What does the song say swept the enemy away?
prompt.older: Comparing Judges 4:13 with Judges 5:21, what swept Sisera's forces away?

choices.text: A great earthquake in the hills

verses.text: So Sisera gathered together all his chariots, nine hundred chariots of iron, and all the people who were with him, from Harosheth Hagoyim to the River Kishon.
The torrent of Kishon swept them away, That ancient torrent, the torrent of Kishon. O my soul, march on in strength!

explanation.adult: Judges 4:13 says where Sisera brought his chariots. Judges 5:21 names the same place in the song.
explanation.child: Read Judges 4:13 and look at where Sisera gathered his army. Then read Judges 5:21.
explanation.teen: The place where Sisera gathered his chariots in 4:13 shows up again in 5:21. Match them up.
explanation.older: The prose account (4:13) names Sisera's staging ground; the poem (5:21) shows that same place turning against him.

teaching.extended_explanation: The song in chapter 5 retells the battle from chapter 4 with poetic details. Look for the place named in both Judges 4:13 and 5:21.
teaching.takeaway: The torrent of Kishon, the very place where Sisera gathered his chariots, swept his forces away.
